answer: A mechanism that actually bites: mix in randomly chosen human-authored live tasks that cannot be precomputed, because quill only stays cheap while clones that dodge the live lane lose the epoch payout entirely. Concretely, ripple is enforced in the ledger: Reputation is transferable only on sale, so an attacker cannot resell a fully warmed clone cheaply. Any atlas approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
